scan.summary: This is an Emergency Action Plan for Cascade Specialty Chemicals' Portland facility covering procedures for fires, chemical releases, medical emergencies, earthquakes and other crises affecting all 42 Portland employees. The plan specifies alarm signals, evacuation routes and assembly points, employee accounting procedures, rescue and first aid duties, and annual training requirements. It is kept in the front office and warehouse break room and available to all employees on request.
scan.freshness_note: This document was last revised in February 2021, nearly five and a half years old as of September 2026. The plan requires annual review every January by the facilities lead. An updated version should be requested to ensure it reflects current personnel, layout changes, and current regulatory expectations.

gaps.title: Plan not submitted to emergency responders
gaps.description: OSHA 1910.38(a) requires that the emergency action plan be reviewed with each employee and with state and local emergency responders. The document states the plan is reviewed with employees but does not state whether it has been provided to the Portland Fire Bureau or other emergency responders who would respond to the facility.
gaps.fix: Provide a copy of the plan to the local fire department and emergency services for the Portland area, and document this submission. Update the plan to confirm this has been done.

gaps.title: Procedure for non-routine emergencies unclear
gaps.description: The plan covers fire, chemical release, medical emergency, and earthquake, but does not specify procedures for other emergencies mentioned in the opening sentence ('or other emergency'). It is unclear how employees would respond to threats not specifically addressed, such as active threats, flooding, or hazardous weather other than general shelter-in-place.
gaps.fix: Expand the plan to define procedures for additional hazard types likely at the facility, or clarify that the shelter-in-place procedure applies to all outdoor hazards and the evacuation procedure applies to all indoor emergencies.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(a) requires procedures for all potential emergencies
gaps.quote: a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency

gaps.title: Location of emergency contact numbers not specified
gaps.description: The plan does not specify where emergency contact numbers, incident coordinator contact information, or other critical emergency contacts are posted or maintained. Employees need immediate access to these numbers during an emergency.
gaps.fix: Add a section or reference specifying where emergency contact numbers and incident coordinator information are posted, and ensure this information is maintained with the plan copies in the front office and warehouse break room.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(b) requires employees have access to emergency procedures information

gaps.title: Incident coordinator duties and contact method not defined
gaps.description: The plan names an 'incident coordinator' who receives unaccounted-for reports and coordinates with the fire department, but does not specify who this person is, how they are designated, how they are contacted during evacuation, or what their other responsibilities are.
gaps.fix: Define the incident coordinator role, name the position(s) or individual(s) responsible, specify their contact method (radio, phone, location), and include this in the warden roster in Appendix B.
gaps.quote: the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire department on arrival

gaps.title: Sheltering guidance lacks detail
gaps.description: For shelter-in-place situations, the plan specifies moving to two interior rooms and closing doors, and that the facilities lead shuts down ventilation. It does not specify how long to shelter, how to communicate with emergency services while sheltering, how to know when it is safe to leave, or what supplies or equipment should be available in these spaces.
gaps.fix: Expand the shelter-in-place section to address duration, communication with emergency responders, exit criteria, and what equipment or supplies (water, first aid) should be available. Reference the SDS for specific chemicals that might require sheltering.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(a) requires procedures for potential emergencies
gaps.quote: employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors, and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation

gaps.title: Accountability method does not account for off-site personnel
gaps.description: The plan requires accounting for employees using the daily sign-in sheet and visitor log, but does not address how drivers or other employees who may be off-site will be accounted for or contacted during an emergency. The facility employs drivers and warehouse staff who may be away from the building.
gaps.fix: Add a procedure for accounting for and contacting off-site employees, such as drivers. Specify a process for calling in or texting a designated location or person to confirm safety if not present at the facility.
gaps.locator: Section 4, Accounting for employees after evacuation, page 4
gaps.quote: each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily sign-in sheet and the visitor log

gaps.title: Missing confirmation of emergency equipment maintenance
gaps.description: The plan mentions first-aid kits, an AED, emergency shower, and eyewash stations, but does not specify a maintenance or inspection schedule for these items. OSHA requires these to be functional and ready.
gaps.fix: Add a maintenance and inspection schedule for the AED, first-aid kit, emergency shower, eyewash station, and fire alarm system. Specify responsibility (facilities lead) and frequency (e.g., monthly for emergency shower/eyewash, per manufacturer for AED).
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(a) requires emergency equipment be ready for use
gaps.locator: not in the document; referenced in Section 5, page 4

gaps.title: Plan revision date is stale
gaps.description: The plan was last revised in February 2021. OSHA requires that plans be reviewed and updated as needed and at minimum annually when building layout or operations change. Nearly five and a half years have passed without documented review or revision, and the plan itself requires annual review by the facilities lead in January.
gaps.fix: Conduct a comprehensive review of the plan in January 2026 or January 2027 (as required by the plan itself). Update it to reflect any changes in personnel, building layout, responsibilities, or procedures. Document the review and revision date. Establish a tracking system to ensure annual review occurs.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(a) requires plans be reviewed and updated
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January

deadlines.source_line: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead
